newsitem.title: USA: Muni dealers propose revised underwriters pact.
newsitem.headline: Muni dealers propose revised underwriters pact.

text.p: PSA The Bond Market Trade Association on Friday proposed changes to the standard pact that firms sign when they join bond syndicates, including new language designed to curb improper political contributions.

The revised "Agreement Among Underwriters" (AAU), does not, however, address recent proposals by the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board Board aimed at tightening disclosure by underwriters and financial advisers, PSA said in announcing the proposal.
PSA wants comments on the draft by Sept 15 and expects to issue a final plan in October.
The proposed revisions come in the midst of a major MSRB review of the way bond deals in the $1.3 trillion muni bond market are financed.
Regulators are concerned about possible conflicts of interest among dealers, financial advisers and other market participants.
PSA said its draft pact addresses new rules adopted by the MSRB and SEC since 1991, when PSA published its last standard agreement.
For instance, changes to the board's rule G-36 require muni dealers to file official statements to the board's electronic repository within certain timeframes.
And rule G-37, adopted by the board in 1994, restricts the political contributions that dealers may make to municipal officials with whom they do bond business.

But PSA said its draft AAU does not address a new round of rule changes proposed recently by MSRB aimed at tightening public disclosures by underwriters and financial advisors that are hired to handle muni deals.
"It is still too early to tell whether, and in what form, those proposals might be adopted," PSA said.
